nyciml-1990-91-spring-seniora-01.title: Cube the equation
nyciml-1990-91-spring-seniora-01.body:
Let $a=\sqrt[3]{26+15\sqrt3}$, $b=\sqrt[3]{26-15\sqrt3}$. Then $a^3+b^3=52$ and $ab=\sqrt[3]{676-675}=1$. Cubing $n=a+b$: $n^3=a^3+b^3+3ab(a+b)=52+3n$, so $n^3-3n-52=(n-4)(n^2+4n+13)=0$. The quadratic has no real roots, so $n=4$.

**Answer: 4**

nyciml-1990-91-spring-seniora-01.title: Recognize perfect cubes
nyciml-1990-91-spring-seniora-01.body:
$(2+\sqrt3)^3=8+12\sqrt3+18+3\sqrt3=26+15\sqrt3$ and similarly $(2-\sqrt3)^3=26-15\sqrt3$. So the sum is $(2+\sqrt3)+(2-\sqrt3)=4$.

**Answer: 4**

nyciml-1990-91-spring-seniora-03.title: Slant height and base
nyciml-1990-91-spring-seniora-03.body:
The semicircle's radius $r$ becomes the slant height, and its arc length $\pi r$ becomes the base circumference, so the base radius is $\frac r2$. The height is $\sqrt{r^2-\frac{r^2}{4}}=\frac{\sqrt3}{2}r$. Volume:
$$\frac13\pi\left(\frac r2\right)^2\cdot\frac{\sqrt3}2r=\frac{\pi\sqrt3\,r^3}{24}.$$

**Answer: $\frac{\pi\sqrt3\,r^3}{24}$**

nyciml-1990-91-spring-seniora-05.title: Roots of unity
nyciml-1990-91-spring-seniora-05.body:
$x+\frac1x=\sqrt3$ gives $x=e^{\pm i\pi/6}$, so $x^3=e^{\pm i\pi/2}=\pm i$ and $x^3+x^{-3}=i+(-i)=0$.

**Answer: 0**

nyciml-1990-91-spring-seniora-06.title: Bound, then test sixths
nyciml-1990-91-spring-seniora-06.body:
Since $6x=7+[x^2]$ is an integer, $x=\frac m6$ for an integer $m$, and $[x^2]=6x-7$ means
$$6x-7\le x^2<6x-6.$$
The left inequality gives $x\le3-\sqrt2\approx1.586$ or $x\ge3+\sqrt2\approx4.414$; the right gives $3-\sqrt3<x<3+\sqrt3$, i.e. $1.268<x<4.732$. So $x\in(1.268,1.586]$ or $x\in[4.414,4.732)$.

With $x=\frac m6$: the first interval gives $m=8,9$ and the second $m=27,28$. So $x=\frac43,\frac32,\frac92,\frac{14}3$. Check, e.g. $x=\frac{14}3$: $[x^2]=[21.8]=21=28-7$.

**Answer: $\frac43,\ \frac32,\ \frac92,\ \frac{14}{3}$**

nyciml-1990-91-spring-seniora-07.title: Quadratic in $x^{3/10}$
nyciml-1990-91-spring-seniora-07.body:
Let $u=x^{3/10}$, so $x^{3/5}=u^2$ and $u^2+7u-8=(u+8)(u-1)=0$. For real $x\ge0$ the principal power $x^{3/10}$ is non-negative, so $u=-8$ is impossible and $u=1$, giving $x^{3}=1$ and $x=1$. (The league's corrected key gives $x=1$, and also accepts the complex cube roots of unity $\frac{-1\pm i\sqrt3}{2}$, which come from $x^3=1$.)

**Answer: $x=1$**

nyciml-1990-91-spring-seniora-08.title: Multiply by cos x
nyciml-1990-91-spring-seniora-08.body:
$61\frac{\sin x}{\cos x}=\frac{60}{\cos x}$ with $\cos x
e0$, so $\sin x=\frac{60}{61}$. Then $|\cos x|=\sqrt{1-\frac{3600}{3721}}=\frac{11}{61}$, and the positive value of $\tan x$ is $\frac{60}{11}$ (in Quadrant I, using the 11-60-61 right triangle).

**Answer: $\frac{60}{11}$**

nyciml-1990-91-spring-seniora-09.title: Explicit roots
nyciml-1990-91-spring-seniora-09.body:
$x=\sqrt2+1$ (or its reciprocal $\sqrt2-1$). Then $x^5=(\sqrt2+1)^5=29\sqrt2+41$ and $x^{-5}=29\sqrt2-41$, so $s_5=58\sqrt2\approx82.02$ and the answer is $82$.

**Answer: 82**

nyciml-1990-91-spring-seniora-10.title: A chord equal to the radius
nyciml-1990-91-spring-seniora-10.body:
Let $AB=\sqrt7$, $BC=2\sqrt{21}$. Each interior angle is $150^\circ$, so
$$AC^2=7+84-2\sqrt7\cdot2\sqrt{21}\cos150^\circ=91+4\cdot7\sqrt3\cdot\frac{\sqrt3}{2}=133.$$
In an inscribed equiangular polygon the sides alternate in length, so each pair of consecutive sides spans $\frac16$ of the circle: $\angle AOC=60^\circ$. Triangle $AOC$ is equilateral, so $r^2=AC^2=133$ and the area is $133\pi$.

**Answer: $133\pi$**

nyciml-1990-91-spring-seniora-12.title: Count each type
nyciml-1990-91-spring-seniora-12.body:
For $n\ge3$: $N(0)=(n-2)^3$, $N(1)=6(n-2)^2$, $N(2)=12(n-2)$, $N(3)=8$. So
$$\frac{N(0)N(2)}{N(1)N(3)}=\frac{12(n-2)^4}{48(n-2)^2}=\frac{(n-2)^2}{4}.$$
(For $n\le2$, $N(1)=0$ and the quotient is undefined.) This is an integer exactly when $n$ is even, and $\frac{(n-2)^2}{4}<1989$ means $n-2<2\sqrt{1989}\approx89.2$, so $n\le90$. The values $n=4,6,\dots,90$ number $44$.

**Answer: 44**

nyciml-1990-91-spring-seniora-13.title: Self-similarity
nyciml-1990-91-spring-seniora-13.body:
Call the value $x>0$. The expression repeats after two radicals: $x=\sqrt{3\sqrt{24x}}$. Then $x^2=3\sqrt{24x}$, $x^4=216x$, $x^3=216$, $x=6$.

**Answer: 6**

nyciml-1990-91-spring-seniora-14.title: Square and check
nyciml-1990-91-spring-seniora-14.body:
Let $t=\tan x$. Squaring and using $\sec^2x=1+t^2$: $9t^2+24t+16=1+t^2$, so $8t^2+24t+15=0$ and $t=\frac{-24\pm\sqrt{96}}{16}=\frac{-6\pm\sqrt6}{4}$.

Both are valid: for $t=\frac{-6+\sqrt6}{4}\approx-0.89$, $\sec x=3t+4\approx1.34$ (a fourth-quadrant angle); for $t=\frac{-6-\sqrt6}{4}\approx-2.11$, $\sec x\approx-2.34$ (a second-quadrant angle). In each case $\sec^2x=1+t^2$ holds, so such an $x$ exists.

**Answer: $\tan x=\frac{-6\pm\sqrt6}{4}$**

nyciml-1990-91-spring-seniora-15.title: Factor
nyciml-1990-91-spring-seniora-15.body:
$42a^2-71ab+30b^2=(6a-5b)(7a-6b)=0$, so $\frac ab=\frac56$ or $\frac67$. The smallest positive solutions are $(5,6)$ with sum $11$ and $(6,7)$ with sum $13$. So $(a,b)=(5,6)$.

**Answer: $(5,6)$**

nyciml-1990-91-spring-seniora-16.title: Change of base
nyciml-1990-91-spring-seniora-16.body:
With $L=\log_217$: $\log_817=\frac L3$ and $\log_{512}17=\frac L9$. The geometric mean is $\sqrt[3]{L\cdot\frac L3\cdot\frac L9}=\frac L3=\log_817$, so $k=8$.

**Answer: 8**

nyciml-1990-91-spring-seniora-16.title: Use reciprocals
nyciml-1990-91-spring-seniora-16.body:
$\log_b17=\frac{1}{\log_{17}b}$, so the condition says $\log_{17}k$ is the geometric mean of $\log_{17}2,\log_{17}8,\log_{17}512$, which are $m,3m,9m$ with geometric mean $3m=\log_{17}8$. So $k=8$.

**Answer: 8**

nyciml-1990-91-spring-seniora-17.title: Step through quarters
nyciml-1990-91-spring-seniora-17.body:
$f$ is non-decreasing and only changes at multiples of $\frac14$. Since $f(x)\approx7x$, look near $x\approx1.4$: on $[\frac54,\frac32)$, $f=1+2+5=8$; on $[\frac32,\frac74)$, $f=1+3+6=10$; on $[\frac74,2)$, $f=1+3+7=11$. So $f(x)=10$ exactly for $\frac32\le x<\frac74$.

**Answer: $\left(\frac32,\frac74\right)$**

nyciml-1990-91-spring-seniora-20.title: Solve for sine and cosine
nyciml-1990-91-spring-seniora-20.body:
From $\sin x=\frac{6-2\cos x}{9}$ and $\sin^2x+\cos^2x=1$: $(6-2c)^2+81c^2=81$, i.e. $85c^2-24c-45=0$, so $c=\frac{24\pm126}{170}$: $c=\frac{15}{17}$ or $c=-\frac35$. Then $\sin x=\frac{8}{17}$ or $\frac45$ respectively (both satisfy the original equation), so $\tan x=\frac{8}{15}$ or $-\frac43$.

**Answer: $\frac{8}{15}$ and $-\frac43$**

nyciml-1990-91-spring-seniora-20.title: Quadratic in tan
nyciml-1990-91-spring-seniora-20.body:
Divide $9\sin x+2\cos x=6$ by $\cos x$ and square, using $\sec^2x=1+t^2$: $(9t+2)^2=36(1+t^2)$, so $45t^2+36t-32=0=(15t-8)(3t+4)$. Each root comes with the sign of $\cos x$ that makes $9\sin x+2\cos x$ positive, so both occur.

**Answer: $\frac{8}{15}$ and $-\frac43$**

nyciml-1990-91-spring-seniora-21.title: Self-similarity
nyciml-1990-91-spring-seniora-21.body:
Call the value $x$. Then $x=\sqrt{3\sqrt[3]{288x}}$, so $x^2=3\sqrt[3]{288x}$ and $x^6=27\cdot288x=7776x$. Thus $x^5=7776=6^5$ and $x=6$.

**Answer: 6**

nyciml-1990-91-spring-seniora-22.title: Factor by grouping
nyciml-1990-91-spring-seniora-22.body:
$x^4-xy^4=x(x^3-y^4)$ and $-\frac{x^3}{y^3}+y=-\frac{x^3-y^4}{y^3}$. So the equation is $(x^3-y^4)\left(x-\frac1{y^3}\right)=0$. Either $x^3=y^4$, giving $\log_yx=\frac43$, or $x=y^{-3}$, giving $\log_yx=-3$.

**Answer: $\frac43$ and $-3$**

nyciml-1990-91-spring-seniora-23.title: Look at one unit interval
nyciml-1990-91-spring-seniora-23.body:
Write $x=k+f$ with $k$ an integer and $0\le f<1$. Then $[2x]+[3x]=5k+[2f]+[3f]$, and $[2f]+[3f]$ takes the values $0,1,2,3$ (for $f$ in $[0,\frac13),[\frac13,\frac12),[\frac12,\frac23),[\frac23,1)$). So the expressible integers are exactly those not $\equiv4\pmod5$. Among $1,\dots,99$, the $20$ numbers $4,9,\dots,99$ are missed, leaving $79$.

**Answer: 79**

nyciml-1990-91-spring-seniora-24.title: Sum over the first experiment
nyciml-1990-91-spring-seniora-24.body:
The first experiment takes $n$ flips with probability $\left(\frac12\right)^n$. The second takes at least $m$ flips exactly when its first $m-1$ flips are tails: probability $\left(\frac12\right)^{m-1}$. So
$$P=\sum_{n\ge1}\left(\frac12\right)^n\left(\frac12\right)^{3n-1}=2\sum_{n\ge1}\left(\frac1{16}\right)^n=2\cdot\frac1{15}=\frac2{15}.$$

**Answer: $\frac{2}{15}$**

nyciml-1990-91-spring-seniora-25.title: Self-similarity
nyciml-1990-91-spring-seniora-25.body:
Let $y=2^x$. The pattern of root indices $2,3,4$ repeats, so $y=\sqrt{2\sqrt[3]{2\sqrt[4]{2y}}}$. In exponents: $y=2^{1/2}\cdot2^{1/6}\cdot2^{1/24}\cdot y^{1/24}$, so $y^{23/24}=2^{17/24}$ and $y=2^{17/23}$. Thus $x=\frac{17}{23}$.

**Answer: $\frac{17}{23}$**

nyciml-1990-91-spring-seniora-26.title: Multiply by z - 1
nyciml-1990-91-spring-seniora-26.body:
$(z-1)(z^4+z^3+z^2+z+1)=z^5-1$, so any root satisfies $z^5=1$ (and $z
e1$ since $1$ is not a root).

**Answer: 1**

nyciml-1990-91-spring-seniora-27.title: Compare powers of 2
nyciml-1990-91-spring-seniora-27.body:
The left side is $3^x2^{3y}$. Factor the smaller power of $2$ from the right side.

If $7x+2y+1<2x+3y-1$ (i.e. $y>5x+2$): the right side is $2^{7x+2y+1}(1+2^{y-5x-2})$. Since $3^x$ is odd, matching powers of $2$ needs $1+2^{y-5x-2}$ odd, so $3y=7x+2y+1$, i.e. $y=7x+1$, and then $3^x=1+2^{2x-1}$. Checking: $x=1$: $3=1+2$ ✓; $x=2$: $9=1+8$ ✓; for $x\ge3$, $2^{2x-1}+1>3^x$ (since $\frac{4^x}{2}$ outgrows $3^x$: $x=3$ gives $33>27$, and the ratio $\frac43$ per step keeps it ahead). So $(1,8)$ and $(2,15)$, both with $y>5x+2$.

If $7x+2y+1>2x+3y-1$: the right side is $2^{2x+3y-1}(1+2^{5x-y+2})$, and matching gives $3y=2x+3y-1$, i.e. $2x=1$, impossible. Equality of the exponents gives $2^{7x+2y+2}$, a pure power of $2$, impossible since $3^x>1$.

**Answer: $(1,8)$ and $(2,15)$**

nyciml-1990-91-spring-seniora-28.title: Solve the system
nyciml-1990-91-spring-seniora-28.body:
Let $g(x)=f(x+1)$. Then $11g(x)+5g(\frac1x)=\log x$, and replacing $x$ by $\frac1x$: $11g(\frac1x)+5g(x)=-\log x$. Adding: $g(x)+g(\frac1x)=0$; subtracting: $6\big(g(x)-g(\frac1x)\big)=2\log x$. Hence $g(x)=\frac{\log x}{6}$, i.e. $f(t)=\frac{\log(t-1)}{6}$.

Then $f(6)+f(17)+f(126)=\frac{\log5+\log16+\log125}{6}=\frac{\log10000}{6}=\frac46=\frac23$.

**Answer: $\frac23$**

nyciml-1990-91-spring-seniora-29.title: Work in units of 1/125
nyciml-1990-91-spring-seniora-29.body:
The left side $F(x)$ is non-decreasing and only jumps at multiples of $\frac1{125}$, so write $x=\frac{m}{125}$. Since $F(x)\approx156x$, $x\approx6.41$. Write $m=125\cdot6+r$:
$$F=6+30+150+750+\left[\tfrac r{125}\right]+\left[\tfrac{r}{25}\right]+\left[\tfrac r5\right]+r=936+\left[\tfrac r{25}\right]+\left[\tfrac r5\right]+r\quad(0\le r<125).$$
We need $r+[\frac r5]+[\frac r{25}]=64$. At $r=52$: $52+10+2=64$; at $r=51$: $51+10+2=63$. So the least $x$ is $\frac{750+52}{125}=6\frac{52}{125}$.

**Answer: $6\frac{52}{125}$**

nyciml-1990-91-spring-seniora-30.title: Conditional probability
nyciml-1990-91-spring-seniora-30.body:
Among the $64$ equally likely sequences, $64-8=56$ have at least one head in the first three tosses. Of the $\binom63=20$ sequences with exactly $3$ heads, only $TTTHHH$ has no head in the first three, leaving $19$. The probability is $\frac{19}{56}$.

**Answer: $\frac{19}{56}$**
